newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Telekom says tariff cuts affect earnings growth.
newsitem.headline: Telekom says tariff cuts affect earnings growth.

text.p: Telekom Malaysia Bhd said on Friday its lower half-year earnings were due to a tariff reduction, slower line installation and a 20 percent increase in operating costs.
"First is the lower than expected revenue growth, attributable to slower line installation coupled with drop in call revenue due to tariff reduction," Telekom said in a statement.

It said the increase in operating cost was attributable to an 8.2 percent rise in labour cost to 419 million ringgit, provision of bad debts totalling 63 million ringgit and increase in interest cost by 71.4 percent to 139 million ringgit.
Telekom reported a net profit of 889.9 million ringgit for the six months to June 30, a 5.7 percent growth over the first half of last year. This compared with a 22.3 percent growth previously.
Telekom said its ATUR 450 cellular phone customers decreased by 4.0 percent to 83,000. "We will however continue this service as a niche market for the advantage of nation-wide coverage," it said.
Telekom said customer base for its other cellular network, TMTouch, is expected to reach 100,000 by the end of the year.
"This company as expected recorded a loss of 49 million ringgit for the first six months of this year. It is still our target that TMTouch will break even in 1999," it said.
